title: AERO9500 Final Report (Part 2) – Space Mission Design
overview: Design a preliminary space mission benefiting Australia and present its space segment (launch, orbit, ground segment, operations, EOL) in a technical report, supported by mission-design software and hand calculations.
deliverables: Single PDF technical report submitted via Turnitin on Moodle
Relevant screenshots included in report or appendix
All relevant STK or PIGI files included with report or appendix

format.length: Maximum 20 pages for core report (excluding title page, table of contents, references, etc.)
format.structure: Executive summary; Introduction (mission overview and rationale); Main body covering space segment (launch, orbit, ground stations, coverage, mission operation, end-of-life); Conclusion; Bibliography
format.other: Clear, effective engineering-report writing style; correct grammar and spelling; clear and logical structure; figures and tables fully and correctly labelled (figure number, title, reference if necessary); all non-original text, diagrams and ideas identified and properly cited/referenced; Wikipedia not accepted as a proper source; report checked for plagiarism

requirements.text: State whether one or multiple spacecraft will be used.
Identify the users, including operator and customers.
Specify the launch site and launch vehicle.
Define the orbit type, its characteristics and orbital elements.
Identify ground control facilities and state how often the spacecraft can communicate with ground control.
State the mission duration and end-of-life (EOL) plans.
Ensure the mission benefits Australia in some way and keep the mission concept simple.
Complete the design using software of choice (STK, PIGI, or other approved software such as flightclub after contacting Naomi), supplementing with hand calculations as needed.
If using PIGI, register for the Saber Astronautics competition to obtain a software license; the design may be entered in the competition.
Contact Naomi before starting work with software other than STK or PIGI.
Include relevant screenshots and all relevant STK or PIGI files with the report or in the appendix.
Cover all main-body space segment topics: launch, orbit, ground stations, coverage, mission operation and end-of-life.
Fully and correctly label figures and tables with number, title and reference if necessary.
Clearly identify and properly cite/reference all text, diagrams, ideas or other information not originating with the student; do not use Wikipedia as a proper source.
